prize_parts.citation: for foundational contributions to the theory of nominal rigidities and monetary policy rules

statement.case_for: Nominal rigidities, staggered price and contract setting, and interest-rate rules are the analytical core of how monetary policy is thought about and conducted. Calvo supplies the tractable time-dependent pricing device, Taylor supplies staggered contracts and the policy rule, and Woodford supplies the microfounded, welfare-based synthesis that turned these pieces into a normative theory of monetary policy. The three contributions are separable, identifiable and mutually reinforcing. Their influence on both theory and central-bank practice has been tested for decades, including through the 2008 crisis and the 2021-23 inflation. Having heard colleagues' arguments, I still judge this to be the strongest combination of conceptual originality, durability and practical consequence among the shortlisted discoveries. I do not treat the opening rankings of other members as scientific evidence in either direction.
statement.case_against: Credit for the New Keynesian framework is diffuse. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets made central contributions to the empirical and medium-scale versions, and a three-name cap necessarily excludes some of them. Several colleagues also note that parts of this territory overlap with earlier prizes on rational expectations, monetary policy and business cycles. The framework's performance in the recent inflation episode and its reliance on representative-agent structure are legitimately debated. The B002 mobility work may offer a cleaner, more novel and arguably more policy-visible discovery with less attribution ambiguity at the level of the programme, although it is younger.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B015 first with a Calvo-Taylor-Woodford core. He concedes that Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler are close behind and that the cut is somewhat arbitrary. He also raises possible overlap with earlier macro prizes.
responses.response: I agree that the cut is a judgement. I would defend this trio because each member is the originator of a distinct building block (pricing, contracts and rules, normative synthesis), whereas the others mainly estimate, extend or apply those blocks. I am less convinced that a Christiano-Eichenbaum variant is better. Medium-scale estimation is a major contribution, but it builds on the blocks rather than introducing them. On overlap, the earlier prizes concern rational expectations and policy evaluation, the real-business-cycle approach and empirical macro methods, not the nominal-rigidity core. Since he and I are long-time collaborators, our agreement on ranking should not be counted as independent corroboration.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B015 last (eighth) because attribution is the weakest aspect, with eight names and a framework built cumulatively. He adds that the three-name cap cannot capture its collective origin and that performance after the 2021-23 inflation is debated.
responses.response: This is the fairest objection to my first choice, and I take it seriously. A collective origin is not by itself disqualifying if the foundational steps can be separated, and I think they can here. The post-2021 debate concerns how well the medium-scale model forecasts, and especially the role of supply shocks and labour-market slack. It does not undermine the Calvo pricing mechanism, the policy-rule logic or the welfare-based normative framework. Where I concede ground is that this is the one candidate where the cap may do real injustice to colleagues. If the committee judges that unacceptable, my alternatives should be read as sincere.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B002 first. She argues that population-scale administrative data plus designs for causal neighbourhood effects changed what can be observed about opportunity, and that the case is strong under common criteria of contribution and impact. She also acknowledges that omitting Katz is a real cost and that some long-run claims are still being tested.
responses.response: I accept that the B002 programme is a major empirical advance and that its measurement and policy reach are exceptional. That is why I list it as an alternative, although I ranked it seventh in my opening view. My remaining hesitation is about maturity and how the contribution is characterised, not quality. The central papers are about a decade old, and the causal reading of place effects is still contested. Her point about Katz also matters, because the cap forces a cleaner but narrower credit story. I would weigh these against the B015 attribution problem rather than treat either as decisive. A newer programme with a contested causal interpretation seems to me a smaller risk than an older one, but it is not negligible.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B002 first and B015 fourth. On B015 he says credit is highly diffuse and that earlier macro prizes cover related ground. On B002 he flags that concentration of credit in Chetty may crowd out others.
responses.response: I agree that diffuse credit is the main weakness of B015, and I do not think the committee should wave it away. I would add that the concentration problem in B002 and the diffusion problem in B015 are mirror images, since both make a three-name allocation contestable. On overlap with earlier prizes, I would distinguish between recognising the same mechanism and recognising the framework that applies those ideas to nominal frictions and policy rules. The latter is, in my reading, not yet fully covered. He should also weigh my disclosed closeness to him as a co-author when reading my reply.

uncertainties: Whether Woodford and Gali, or Calvo and Taylor, should be treated as the better pair of foundational contributions if the committee wants fewer than three names.
How much weight the committee should give to the post-2021 inflation experience in assessing the lasting value of the framework.
Whether B002 maturity concerns (core work from about 2014 to 2022, contested causal reading of place effects) should be weighed more heavily than B015 attribution concerns.
Whether the exclusion of Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets can be justified as a principled distinction between originators of building blocks and developers of estimated versions.
statement.conflict_note: No credited name on B015 is a co-author of mine according to my profile. Disclosed connections: I have co-authored with John Hassler (chair), who also ranked B015 first, and with Timo Boppart (co-opted member). I am a long-term co-author of Giovanni Violante (credited on B005, which I do not propose). I have also worked on capital-skill complementarity, which is adjacent to B024, and on heterogeneous-agent methods, which are adjacent to B005. None of these is adjudicated here.
